taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, using only the rule descriptions provided.

## 1. Loop-drawing puzzles
These require drawing a single continuous loop through cells or dots.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop through cell centers; must pass white circles and avoid black circles.
- **Masyu** — single loop through cell centers; passes through black and white circles with turn/straight constraints.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop through cells; must pass through all black circles as midpoints of straight segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop through cells; must visit rooms in a specific moon/sun alternation pattern.
- **Nagareru** — single directed loop; must follow arrow direction and wind constraints.
- **Slitherlink** — single loop on dot grid; numbers indicate surrounding line count.
- **Suraromu** — single loop through cells; must pass all gates in order from a numbered start.
- **Yajilin** — single loop through cells; black cells are placed separately and numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction.

## 2. Region-filling / shading puzzles
These involve coloring cells black/white or otherwise partitioning the grid into regions.

- **Akari** — place light bulbs so all white cells are illuminated.
- **Choco Banana** — paint some cells black so black areas are rectangles/squares and white areas are not.
- **Heyawake** — paint cells black with room counts and connectivity restrictions.
- **Hitori** — blacken cells so numbers don’t repeat in rows/columns; white cells stay connected.
- **Kurodoko** — blacken cells so numbered cells see a certain number of white cells.
- **Nurikabe** — black cells form one wall; white areas are numbered islands.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint walls to create a maze from S to G with room constraints.
- **Nurimisaki** — fill cells so “Misaki” cells form straight white promontories.
- **Norinori** — place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles in squares so remaining white forms rectangles/squares.
- **Sto-stone** — fill colored cells so room counts and “dropped” stones satisfy constraints.
- **Usowan** — color cells with exactly one wrong number per room.
- **Tilepaint** — color tiles so the solution outlines an object.

## 3. Number-placement puzzles
These require filling cells with numbers under structural constraints.

- **Fillomino** — fill all cells with numbers; each block size matches its number.
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into blocks of five cells with line-count clues.
- **Juosan** — fill cells with horizontal or vertical marks under territory counts.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers; arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with numbers from a given list.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1; duplicates in rows/columns must be spaced apart.
- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles, each containing one number equal to its area.
- **Sudoku** — fill grid with 1–9 so rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks contain all digits.
- **Usowan** — also includes number interpretation, but the core task is shading with number clues.

## 4. Connectivity / path-linking puzzles
These involve connecting pairs, islands, or endpoints with lines or bridges.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges.
- **Numberlink** — connect matching number pairs with non-crossing lines.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles so each country contains one circle; circles travel along tracks.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas; arrows show movement paths and gray-area sums.

## 5. Shape / block-formation puzzles
These focus on forming specific shapes or blocks.

- **Chained Block** — fill black-cell blocks; each block has a number or “?” and blocks form chains.
- **Double Choco** — divide grid into blocks containing matching white and gray areas of same shape.
- **Evolomino** — draw squares in white cells so blocks grow by one square along arrows.
- **LITS** — color tetrominoes in each room; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch except at corners.
- **Nuritwin** — shade cells so each region contains exactly two equal-sized blocks.
- **Pencils** — mark pencil shapes and draw lines from tips through numbered lengths.
- **Sashigane** — divide grid into L-shaped blocks with arrows/open circles indicating block structure.

## 6. Circle / clue-based local constraint puzzles
These use circles, arrows, or local numeric clues to constrain nearby cells.

- **Hebi** — place snake numbers 1 to 5; black-cell arrows give directional visibility counts.
- **Kurotto** — circle numbers indicate the sum of continuous black cells extending from the circle.
- **Makaro** — black arrows indicate the largest adjacent number in the pointed direction.
- **Nurimisaki** — circles mark Misaki cells and numbers indicate straight-line white length.
- **Yajilin** — arrow numbers indicate black cells in that direction.
- **Yosenabe** — circles move into gray areas; gray numbers equal total entering circle values.

## 7. Room-based puzzles
These are organized around bold-line bounded rooms.

- **Double Choco** — blocks must contain paired white/gray areas of same form.
- **Heyawake** — rooms have painted-cell counts and white-cell path restrictions.
- **Juosan** — territories have counts of horizontal/vertical marks.
- **Makaro** — rooms contain consecutive numbers and arrow constraints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — rooms must contain all moons or all suns, with alternation between rooms.
- **Nurimeizu** — rooms must be uniformly painted or white.
- **Nuritwin** — outlined regions each contain two equal blocks.
- **Ripple Effect** — rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1.
- **Shikaku** — rectangles are formed around numbers.
- **Sto-stone** — rooms contain a specified number of continuous black cells.
- **Usowan** — each room has exactly one wrong number.
- **Choco Banana** — black/white regions are constrained by shape, though not explicitly room-based in the same way.

## 8. Arrow-direction puzzles
These use arrows as primary directional constraints.

- **Hebi** — black-cell arrows indicate visibility direction.
- **Makaro** — black arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Nagareru** — arrows define the loop’s direction and wind behavior.
- **Pencils** — pencil tips define line direction and length.
- **Sashigane** — arrows point toward the knee of an L-shaped block.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move along tracks; arrows show movement paths in the sample.
- **Suraromu** — gates and numbered start determine loop order.
- **Yajilin** — arrows indicate how many black cells lie in that direction.
- **Yosenabe** — arrows show how circles move into gray areas.

## 9. Adjacency / separation constraint puzzles
These emphasize what may or may not touch.

- **Akari** — bulbs cannot illuminate another bulb.
- **Chained Block** — blocks in a chain cannot repeat the same shape.
- **Double Choco** — paired areas must match in shape.
- **Fillomino** — same-sized blocks cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Hitori** — black cells cannot touch; white cells must connect.
- **Kurodoko** — black cells cannot touch; white cells must connect.
- **LITS** — same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch except at corners.
- **Nurikabe** — black cells form one wall; 2×2 black forbidden.
- **Nurimisaki** — black and white 2×2 or larger squares forbidden.
- **Nuritwin** — shaded blocks in same region cannot touch; 2×2 all-shaded forbidden.
- **Shakashaka** — white remainder must form rectangles/squares.
- **Usowan** — colored cells cannot touch; white cells must stay connected.
- **Yajilin** — black cells cannot touch; loop avoids them.

If you want, I can also turn this into:
1. a **table**,  
2. a **hierarchical tree**, or  
3. a **taxonomy by primary mechanic + secondary constraint**.
